# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
    secrets: inherit

run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # gh-676: Phantom push-event AI Teammate runs on factory-data (no trigger, no jobs, instant failure)

## Description

## Symptom

Every SM state push to `factory-data` fires an AI Teammate run with `event=push` that fails instantly with **zero jobs and no retained logs**:

- 20:01:24 and 20:01:34 (run 37150034245) — `factory state — <timestamp>`
- 19:05 ×2, plus pairs every ~30m since ~18:30
- API: `path=.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml, head_branch=factory-data, event=push`; `gh run view --log` → "log not found"

## Why impossible

`ai-teammate.yml` has **no `push:` trigger** (only `issues` + `workflow_dispatch`). This is the classic **phantom workflow registration**: the stub was unparseable for a stretch today (duplicate permission keys, #671), and GitHub kept a path-named registration that still matches push events.

## Fix direction

1. Verify whether the phantom dies on its own now that the file is valid on main (if runs stop after the next factory-data push + a workflow-file touch, document and close).
2. If it persists: the standard cure is a no-op commit touching `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` (forces GitHub to re-index the registration); verify event=push runs stop.
3. Confirm no real trigger semantics are lost (issues/dispatch must keep firing).

## Impact

Noise (~2 failed runs / 30m), no runner cost (0 jobs), but it pollutes run history and can trip failure-based watchdogs (ours did).

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37150447894) · started 20:10 · done 20:23 ✅

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
    secrets: inherit

run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

# gh-676: Phantom push-event AI Teammate runs on factory-data (no trigger, no jobs, instant failure)

## Description

## Symptom

Every SM state push to `factory-data` fires an AI Teammate run with `event=push` that fails instantly with **zero jobs and no retained logs**:

- 20:01:24 and 20:01:34 (run 37150034245) — `factory state — <timestamp>`
- 19:05 ×2, plus pairs every ~30m since ~18:30
- API: `path=.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml, head_branch=factory-data, event=push`; `gh run view --log` → "log not found"

## Why impossible

`ai-teammate.yml` has **no `push:` trigger** (only `issues` + `workflow_dispatch`). This is the classic **phantom workflow registration**: the stub was unparseable for a stretch today (duplicate permission keys, #671), and GitHub kept a path-named registration that still matches push events.

## Fix direction

1. Verify whether the phantom dies on its own now that the file is valid on main (if runs stop after the next factory-data push + a workflow-file touch, document and close).
2. If it persists: the standard cure is a no-op commit touching `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` (forces GitHub to re-index the registration); verify event=push runs stop.
3. Confirm no real trigger semantics are lost (issues/dispatch must keep firing).

## Impact

Noise (~2 failed runs / 30m), no runner cost (0 jobs), but it pollutes run history and can trip failure-based watchdogs (ours did).

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37150447894) · started 20:10 · done 20:23 ✅

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
    secrets: inherit

run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

💡 **SUGGESTION: Block-scalar detection misses trailing comments → false duplicate-key alarms**

`BLOCK_SCALAR_RE` is tested against the raw value, so a legal trailing comment on a block-scalar introducer defeats scalar detection:

```yaml
- run: | # note: keep env inline   ← BLOCK_SCALAR_RE does not match "…| # note"
    FOO: bar
    FOO: baz
```

Here the scalar content is parsed as YAML keys and `findDuplicateKeys` reports a false duplicate (verified against this module: `[{"key":"FOO","line":6}]`), which would fail the repo-wide R2 scan on a perfectly valid workflow. Shell content with repeated `KEY: value` lines (curl headers, env blocks) is the realistic trigger.

Strip a trailing comment before the test:

```js
if (m[3] && BLOCK_SCALAR_RE.test(m[3].trim().replace(/[ \t]+#.*$/, ''))) {
    scalarIndent = indent;
}
```

The same `#`-strip that `extractTriggers` already applies to the `on:` line would do. Current `.github/workflows/*.yml` all pass, so this is polish, not a blocker.

💡 **SUGGESTION: A column-0 comment inside the `on:` block terminates trigger extraction**

The block-form scan breaks on any line at indent 0, including full-line comments:

```yaml
on:
  issues:
# why: no push trigger by design   ← legal YAML, but `indent === 0` breaks here
  workflow_dispatch:
```

`extractTriggers` then returns `['issues']` and the R1 contract test fails on a semantically correct file — a false alarm rather than a silent pass (fail-safe direction), but it would send a future reformat into a confusing rework loop. The file's own header comment style makes a column-0 note inside `on:` plausible someday.

Consider skipping full-line comments at indent 0 instead of treating them as the block terminator (skip `#`-leading lines before the `indent === 0` check); dedent to a real key remains the terminator.

# gh-676: Phantom push-event AI Teammate runs on factory-data (no trigger, no jobs, instant failure)

## Description

## Symptom

Every SM state push to `factory-data` fires an AI Teammate run with `event=push` that fails instantly with **zero jobs and no retained logs**:

- 20:01:24 and 20:01:34 (run 37150034245) — `factory state — <timestamp>`
- 19:05 ×2, plus pairs every ~30m since ~18:30
- API: `path=.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml, head_branch=factory-data, event=push`; `gh run view --log` → "log not found"

## Why impossible

`ai-teammate.yml` has **no `push:` trigger** (only `issues` + `workflow_dispatch`). This is the classic **phantom workflow registration**: the stub was unparseable for a stretch today (duplicate permission keys, #671), and GitHub kept a path-named registration that still matches push events.

## Fix direction

1. Verify whether the phantom dies on its own now that the file is valid on main (if runs stop after the next factory-data push + a workflow-file touch, document and close).
2. If it persists: the standard cure is a no-op commit touching `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` (forces GitHub to re-index the registration); verify event=push runs stop.
3. Confirm no real trigger semantics are lost (issues/dispatch must keep firing).

## Impact

Noise (~2 failed runs / 30m), no runner cost (0 jobs), but it pollutes run history and can trip failure-based watchdogs (ours did).

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37150447894) · started 20:10 · done 20:23 ✅

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure
- `metadata.contextId` identifies the workflow (used for config composition lookups).
- `preJSAction` / `preCliJSAction` / `postJSAction` — GraalJS hooks that run before/after the CLI agent.
- `cliPrompt` — path to the main prompt markdown.
- `cliPrompts` — additional prompt files appended to the CLI agent input.
- `cliCommands` — shell scripts invoked by dmtools to run the AI CLI.

### Label-based idempotency
SM rules use `skipIfLabel` / `addLabel` to prevent re-processing tickets. When adding new rules, always include an idempotency label.

### SCM abstraction
Use `js/common/scm.js` (via `configLoader.createScm(config)`) instead of calling `github_*` or `ado_*` globals directly. This keeps agents portable between GitHub and Azure DevOps.

### Config composition
Project repos customize agent behavior through `.dmtools/config.js` fields:
- `cliPrompts.<contextId>` — append prompt files to a specific agent's CLI input
- `cliPromptOverrides.<contextId>` — replace the entry prompt for a specific agent
- `additionalInstructions.<contextId>` — append to `agentParams.instructions` for a specific agent

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
    secrets: inherit

run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Block-scalar detection misses trailing comments → false duplicate-key alarms**

`BLOCK_SCALAR_RE` is tested against the raw value, so a legal trailing comment on a block-scalar introducer defeats scalar detection:

```yaml
- run: | # note: keep env inline   ← BLOCK_SCALAR_RE does not match "…| # note"
    FOO: bar
    FOO: baz
```

Here the scalar content is parsed as YAML keys and `findDuplicateKeys` reports a false duplicate (verified against this module: `[{"key":"FOO","line":6}]`), which would fail the repo-wide R2 scan on a perfectly valid workflow. Shell content with repeated `KEY: value` lines (curl headers, env blocks) is the realistic trigger.

Strip a trailing comment before the test:

```js
if (m[3] && BLOCK_SCALAR_RE.test(m[3].trim().replace(/[ \t]+#.*$/, ''))) {
    scalarIndent = indent;
}
```

The same `#`-strip that `extractTriggers` already applies to the `on:` line would do. Current `.github/workflows/*.yml` all pass, so this is polish, not a blocker.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: A column-0 comment inside the `on:` block terminates trigger extraction**

The block-form scan breaks on any line at indent 0, including full-line comments:

```yaml
on:
  issues:
# why: no push trigger by design   ← legal YAML, but `indent === 0` breaks here
  workflow_dispatch:
```

`extractTriggers` then returns `['issues']` and the R1 contract test fails on a semantically correct file — a false alarm rather than a silent pass (fail-safe direction), but it would send a future reformat into a confusing rework loop. The file's own header comment style makes a column-0 note inside `on:` plausible someday.

Consider skipping full-line comments at indent 0 instead of treating them as the block terminator (skip `#`-leading lines before the `indent === 0` check); dedent to a real key remains the terminator.
"}

💡 **SUGGESTION: Top-level `file_read` calls are unguarded — a missing file crashes the whole suite at load**

`STUB`/`TEMPLATE` are read at module top level, outside any `test()`:

```js
var STUB = file_read({ path: '.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml' });
var TEMPLATE = file_read({ path: 'workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template' });
```

If either file is missing/renamed, `file_read` throws during load and every suite in the run dies with it (the node-harness coverage run in `quality.yml` would lose all coverage for the file). Contrast: the `file_list` branch below IS guarded with a `typeof` check and degrades gracefully.

AGENTS.md asks suites to degrade gracefully in standalone context. Suggested shape: assert existence as the first contract test (`assert.ok(STUB, 'stub missing — the machine loop would be dead')`) or wrap in try/catch and skip with a loud message. Hard-failing when the stub is gone is the right *intent* — just do it inside a test, not at load time.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `.fah/memory/` files are not mentioned in the PR description**

This PR ships three `.fah/memory/` files (`.gitattributes` with union-merge drivers, `.gitignore` for derivatives, and note `n_0001_2f7c.md`) that are unrelated to the gh-676 phantom fix and absent from the PR description's "What changed". Content is generic and the union-merge setup looks like deliberate harness design, so nothing to remove — but a one-line mention in the description (or a separate commit) would keep the gh-676 diff self-explanatory for anyone doing archaeology on the incident.

Note the committed note itself documents the exact hazard that makes this review's top general-comment item urgent: the dev loop auto-commits the working tree every 5 minutes, so scratch/runtime files left in the tree (e.g. staged `.dmtools/*.log`) ship silently on the next WIP save.

## PR Description

### What changed

Kills the gh-676 phantom (`event=push` AI Teammate runs on `factory-data`, 0 jobs, instant fail): a **no-op comment touch of `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`** — the default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the workflow registration from the real triggers, discarding the stale push registration left over from the #671 unparseable window — plus a regression guard (`js/workflowLint.js` + `js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js`, 24 tests) locking the stub's trigger set to exactly `issues` + `workflow_dispatch` and banning duplicate YAML keys across all `.github/workflows/*.yml`.

### Key decisions

- Cure over observation: the touch satisfies both fix paths — if the phantom was already dying, the touch is harmless; if not, it is the standard re-index trigger. Zero semantic change (triggers/jobs untouched, verified by tests).
- Guard targets the root-cause class, not the symptom: duplicate keys (the #669/#671 residue) are what made the file unparseable and bred the phantom; a strict indent-aware scanner (list-item and block-scalar aware) now fails any PR introducing them. Cross-checked against the original #671 breakage shape and a real YAML parser.
- Exact trigger-set match (not substring checks) for the stub and `workflows/ai-teammate.yml.template`: an added `push:` trigger would launch teammate runs on every SM state push; a dropped one silently kills the machine loop.
- `.gitignore` now excludes `.dmtools/*.log` runtime artifacts (credential-helper traces were at risk of being committed by the WIP auto-save).

### How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_workflowLint.json   # 24 tests — triggers + duplicate-key scan
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json            # full suite: 1346 passed, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
  MERGE[PR merge → ai-teammate.yml blob change on main] --> REINDEX[GitHub re-indexes workflow registration]
```

# gh-676: Phantom push-event AI Teammate runs on factory-data (no trigger, no jobs, instant failure)

## Description

## Symptom

Every SM state push to `factory-data` fires an AI Teammate run with `event=push` that fails instantly with **zero jobs and no retained logs**:

- 20:01:24 and 20:01:34 (run 37150034245) — `factory state — <timestamp>`
- 19:05 ×2, plus pairs every ~30m since ~18:30
- API: `path=.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml, head_branch=factory-data, event=push`; `gh run view --log` → "log not found"

## Why impossible

`ai-teammate.yml` has **no `push:` trigger** (only `issues` + `workflow_dispatch`). This is the classic **phantom workflow registration**: the stub was unparseable for a stretch today (duplicate permission keys, #671), and GitHub kept a path-named registration that still matches push events.

## Fix direction

1. Verify whether the phantom dies on its own now that the file is valid on main (if runs stop after the next factory-data push + a workflow-file touch, document and close).
2. If it persists: the standard cure is a no-op commit touching `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` (forces GitHub to re-index the registration); verify event=push runs stop.
3. Confirm no real trigger semantics are lost (issues/dispatch must keep firing).

## Impact

Noise (~2 failed runs / 30m), no runner cost (0 jobs), but it pollutes run history and can trip failure-based watchdogs (ours did).

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37150447894) · started 20:10 · done 20:23 ✅

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo — never here.

**Before every commit**: re-read your diff and check it against this list.

### Agent config structure

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows),
# SELF-HOSTED ENGINE: this repo IS the dmtools-agents engine, so factory_ref
# rides the triggering commit — the factory always executes the exact tree
# under development.
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries the repository event triggers + the call only.
#
# Gate: the loop starts when a human ASSIGNS an issue to `ai-teammate`.
# Secrets via `secrets: inherit`: SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (present), plus
# ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY when the fa/zai runners are used.
#
# gh-676 (2026-10-03): while this file was unparseable (#669 residue —
# duplicate permission keys, fixed in #671), GitHub kept a stale push-event
# registration: every machine-sm state-publish push to `factory-data`
# spawned an instant-fail event=push run with zero jobs ("the phantom").
# This comment block is the standard cure — a no-op touch of the file: the
# default-branch blob change forces GitHub to re-index the registration
# from the real triggers below. There is NO push trigger by design; the
# trigger set (issues + workflow_dispatch only) and the duplicate-key
# ban are guarded by js/unit-tests/test_workflowLint.js.
name: AI Teammate

run-name: "teammate: ${{ github.event_name }} #${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }} ${{ github.event.inputs.leg }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (for dispatch runs)'
        type: string
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why (audit trail)'
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored runs (review leg on PRs born without an issue, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read' — the issue-
  # driven dev lane never ran in this repo).
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  group: ai-teammate-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  teammate:
    # Assignment gate: issues must be ASSIGNED to ai-teammate; dispatch
    # runs reach the factory even with empty gate outputs.
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       contains(github.event.issue.assignees.*.login, 'ai-teammate')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'issues' &&
       github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved') ||
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: 'ai-teammate'
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || github.event_name }}
      factory_ref: ${{ github.sha }}
    secrets: inherit

run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # The harness expects the consumer layout (agents/ checkout beside
          # the cwd) and bare config names — self-symlink covers both.
          ln -sfn "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/agents"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # The node harness is a degraded mirror of the dmtools runner
        # (~108 known mock-gap failures, e.g. cli_execute_command stubs);
        # the canonical green-gate is the pack-release test job. Coverage is
        # collected regardless — a red harness must not block the ratchet.
        # ci/run_with_coverage.js wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul
        # global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES \
            || echo "::warning::node harness has known mock gaps — coverage still collected"

      - name: crap4js gate (ratchet — baseline ${{ env.CRAP_THRESHOLD }})
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}"

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Block-scalar detection misses trailing comments → false duplicate-key alarms**

`BLOCK_SCALAR_RE` is tested against the raw value, so a legal trailing comment on a block-scalar introducer defeats scalar detection:

```yaml
- run: | # note: keep env inline   ← BLOCK_SCALAR_RE does not match "…| # note"
    FOO: bar
    FOO: baz
```

Here the scalar content is parsed as YAML keys and `findDuplicateKeys` reports a false duplicate (verified against this module: `[{"key":"FOO","line":6}]`), which would fail the repo-wide R2 scan on a perfectly valid workflow. Shell content with repeated `KEY: value` lines (curl headers, env blocks) is the realistic trigger.

Strip a trailing comment before the test:

```js
if (m[3] && BLOCK_SCALAR_RE.test(m[3].trim().replace(/[ \t]+#.*$/, ''))) {
    scalarIndent = indent;
}
```

The same `#`-strip that `extractTriggers` already applies to the `on:` line would do. Current `.github/workflows/*.yml` all pass, so this is polish, not a blocker.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: A column-0 comment inside the `on:` block terminates trigger extraction**

The block-form scan breaks on any line at indent 0, including full-line comments:

```yaml
on:
  issues:
# why: no push trigger by design   ← legal YAML, but `indent === 0` breaks here
  workflow_dispatch:
```

`extractTriggers` then returns `['issues']` and the R1 contract test fails on a semantically correct file — a false alarm rather than a silent pass (fail-safe direction), but it would send a future reformat into a confusing rework loop. The file's own header comment style makes a column-0 note inside `on:` plausible someday.

Consider skipping full-line comments at indent 0 instead of treating them as the block terminator (skip `#`-leading lines before the `indent === 0` check); dedent to a real key remains the terminator.
"}

# gh-676: Phantom push-event AI Teammate runs on factory-data (no trigger, no jobs, instant failure)

## Description

## Symptom

Every SM state push to `factory-data` fires an AI Teammate run with `event=push` that fails instantly with **zero jobs and no retained logs**:

- 20:01:24 and 20:01:34 (run 37150034245) — `factory state — <timestamp>`
- 19:05 ×2, plus pairs every ~30m since ~18:30
- API: `path=.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml, head_branch=factory-data, event=push`; `gh run view --log` → "log not found"

## Why impossible

`ai-teammate.yml` has **no `push:` trigger** (only `issues` + `workflow_dispatch`). This is the classic **phantom workflow registration**: the stub was unparseable for a stretch today (duplicate permission keys, #671), and GitHub kept a path-named registration that still matches push events.

## Fix direction

1. Verify whether the phantom dies on its own now that the file is valid on main (if runs stop after the next factory-data push + a workflow-file touch, document and close).
2. If it persists: the standard cure is a no-op commit touching `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` (forces GitHub to re-index the registration); verify event=push runs stop.
3. Confirm no real trigger semantics are lost (issues/dispatch must keep firing).

## Impact

Noise (~2 failed runs / 30m), no runner cost (0 jobs), but it pollutes run history and can trip failure-based watchdogs (ours did).

## Machine jobs
- [x] ▶ dev (fa-story-dev) · [run](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/37150447894) · started 20:10 · done 20:23 ✅
